note.title: An imagined story
note.p1: Ghafla is a work of fiction. The character, his dream, the world he walks through and the places where he finds the pages are all invented, to illustrate one idea: heedlessness (ghafla) can overtake us quietly, and it is never too late to come back.
note.p2: It is neither religious teaching nor a judgement on how other people practise. The game judges no one and mocks nothing: to learn about the religion, turn to people of knowledge and read the Quran itself.
note.p3: The text of the Quran is never written by hand in the game: pages are displayed from a recognised text source, or only suggested by lines if the text is not available. Quoted verses are given from The Clear Quran by Dr. Mustafa Khattab, with their reference: a translation helps understanding, but the Quran itself is in Arabic.
note.p4: By design, there are no faces, no statues, no images of people, and no music.
note.download: Download: during the opening cinematic, the game can download the text of the whole Mushaf (604 pages, about 2 MB, once only, Internet connection required). It is kept on the device; without it, the book's pages show only lines.
